questions.question: Explain the difference between a movement along a demand curve and a shift of the demand curve.
questions.expected_answer: A movement along the curve is caused only by a change in the price of the good itself. A shift of the curve is caused by a change in non-price factors, such as consumer income or preferences.

questions.question: Describe what happens in a market when the price is set below the equilibrium price.
questions.expected_answer: When the price is below equilibrium, the quantity demanded exceeds the quantity supplied, creating a shortage. This shortage drives the price up until equilibrium is restored.

questions.question: If consumer income increases, walk through the step-by-step impact on the market for a normal good like beef.
questions.expected_answer: Since beef is a normal good, an increase in income shifts the demand curve to the right. The supply curve stays the same. The new intersection point represents a higher equilibrium price and a higher equilibrium quantity.
